content.text: The bug is in `parseDate`: `Date.UTC` takes a 0-indexed month, but the ISO month is 1-indexed.

content.content: The file /work/.tmp/claude-eval-vNTYd2/home/cwd/src/dates.js has been updated successfully.

lines: // Parse an ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) into a UTC Date.

content.text:
I fixed it, and `npm test` now passes.

**Cause:** `parseDate` in `src/dates.js` passed the ISO month straight to `Date.UTC`, which counts months from 0. Every parsed date landed one month late, so an invoice issued Jan 30 was treated as Feb 30, which rolls over to Mar 2. Adding 14 days then gave 2026-03-16 instead of 2026-02-13.

**Fix:** `Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d)`.

`reportMonth` in `src/report.js` also uses `parseDate` and already adds 1 to the month. It was showing the wrong month label before and is correct now, so it needs no change.

The only test is the one net-14 case. It doesn't cover other months or year boundaries, so I haven't tested those.
